candidate_profile.description: The candidate treats the case as a generic grocery profitability problem, does not focus on private label mix, and fails to test whether management's 3-point penetration plan is enough to hit the profit target.
behaviour_rules: Do not anchor clearly on the 10% profit increase target of $180M.
Ask few or no useful clarification questions about product mix, margin differences, or store-level pervasiveness.
Suggest weak solutions such as closing stores or expanding geographically even though the case guidance rules those out.
Use a generic profitability framework without prioritizing private label versus national brand economics.
Do not connect stagnating private label growth to stagnating profits.
Miss that private label brands likely carry structurally better margins than national brands.
Fail to calculate the profit impact of a 3 percentage point increase in private label penetration.
End with a vague recommendation such as cut costs or market more private label, without showing whether the target is actually achievable.

expected_issues: Fails to recognize that profitability is a broad issue across stores and that closures are not the intended answer.
Does not connect private label stagnation to profit stagnation.
Misses the importance of the gross margin gap between private label and national brands.
Fails to calculate whether a 3 percentage point private label penetration increase exceeds the $180M target.
Does not account for taxes when estimating profit impact.
Recommendation is generic and not tied to management's concrete hypothesis.
expected_feedback_points: Focus on mix and margin rather than store closures or near-term geographic expansion.
Use the exhibit to connect private label growth with profit growth historically.
Test management's hypothesis quantitatively against the $180M target.
Recognize that only COGS and taxes change in the private label shift scenario.
Recommend validating the 3-point penetration assumption and understanding one-time execution costs.
